**My reasoning:**

I've farmed this land outside Quzhou for over 50 years. My father farmed it before me. At 70, my knees don't hold up like they used to, so I can't manage too much myself — my son helps during the busy harvest. I have about 8 mu total.

In Quzhou, everybody grows wheat and maize. That's what the land is good for, that's what the buyers want, and that's what I know how to grow. I'm not going to try cotton or vegetables at my age — too much fuss. The wheat goes in October after I deal with the maize stubble, and the maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June. Same rotation I've done my whole life.

For wheat seed, I'll use the improved Jimai variety the village co-op sells. It yields well and the county extension office has been pushing it. For maize I always use Zhengdan 958 hybrid — everyone uses it, it's reliable.

I apply fertilizer in the way I've always done: base fertilizer before wheat planting, then top-dress in spring. I'd rather put a bit more down than have a poor harvest. Groundwater is still accessible on my well, so I'll irrigate five times for the wheat — it needs it in winter and spring. Maize gets rain in summer mostly, so maybe twice.

I use rotary tillage both seasons. I can hire the machine from the village service station for 30 yuan a mu. No-tillage sounds risky to me — I don't trust it.
